scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Voice of the Sun
This is Lusheng Dance. Tang Dynasty to present.
on_screen: Title card: Lusheng Dance · China · Tang Dynasty to present

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The lusheng is traced back 3000 years to the Tang Dynasty, with origins in the Central Plains.
The oldest written description of the Miao lusheng dance dates to 1664 by Lu Tze Yun, who observed courtship dances involving men playing six-pipe instruments.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Used for courtship, funeral rites, and the annual Lusheng Festival.
It is considered a spiritual instrument that connects the living to ancestors and the divine.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Men play the lusheng while moving, often swinging the instrument side-to-side.
Women dance in concentric circles.
The dance is performed in ritualized forms during festivals and as a courtship activity in designated fields.
Watch for Instrument swinging.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The lusheng is a polyphonic mouth-organ with 5-6 bamboo pipes and a hardwood air chamber (sheng dou).
It produces a bright, multi-tonal sound.
Listen for the Lusheng (bamboo mouth-organ).
A polyphonic, bright, and resonant sound produced by multiple bamboo pipes of varying lengths, often played in groups to create a layered, harmonic texture.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
scenes.music: the music brief's underscore at its own tempo; drop narration under the hook of a verified recording if licensed, else original

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Women wear silver-decorated costumes.
The dance takes place in 'lusheng fields' in Miao villages or during festivals.
Instruments are often decorated with red ribbons when they win competitions.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Variants exist among the Dong, Yao, Zhuang, Bouyei, and Lahu.
Evolved from the ancient Chinese 'Yu' and related to the 'sheng' family of free-reed instruments.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Lusheng Dance is parent of Sheng: The lusheng is considered a regional evolution of the ancient sheng family.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Playing is prohibited between spring and autumn harvest; instruments must be wrapped in red cloth and stored to avoid offending the gods.

narration: Discover the Lusheng Dance, a sacred Miao tradition where bamboo music bridges the gap between the living and the divine.
